title: Repair Bias in Data
outcome: By the end, I can distinguish a biased collection process from a mere small dataset.
scenario: A fictional school polls learners about adding comic recommendations.
given: Library-club respondents: 12 Yes out of 15. Other respondents: 3 Yes out of 15.
The full grade has 30 club members and 90 others. These respondents were volunteers, not random selections.

steps.label: Check representation
steps.detail: Respondents split 50/50, but the grade is 25% club and 75% other.

steps.label: Repair collection
steps.detail: Plan including equality, documented invitations and report nonresponse by group.

explanation: The combined respondent result gives club members more influence than their share of the grade. A weighted illustration using 25% and 75% gives 0.25×80%+0.75×20%=35%, but volunteers may differ within each group, so weighting alone does not establish the true grade preference. Improve the collection process rather than announcing the weighted number as fact.

counterfactual.prediction: Sample size increases without fixing missing representation of other learners.
counterfactual.reason: The added respondents come from the already overrepresented group.

student_task: Why must 35% be labelled an illustration rather than the measured grade-wide Yes rate?
teacher_answer: It assumes each volunteer group rate represents its whole group; that assumption has not been established.
project_evidence: Broaden recommender feedback collection and show respondent group coverage before making user-preference claims.
limits: Neither raw nor weighted volunteer rates prove the whole grade’s opinion; privacy and consent rules still apply.
review_note: New fictional case individually matched to this topic, with computations and policy traces checked. Use for supported practice; preserve the independent assessment.
